summary: Explainers, tutorials and how-things-work videos. Viewers come to learn one thing; retention depends on a clear promise, one idea per scene and visible progress.

archetypes.name: Problem, insight, steps, recap
archetypes.when_to_use: Teaching a skill or concept in 30 to 180 seconds.

structure.goal: State the surprising fact or the outcome the viewer will have
Show the common misconception or pain
structure.notes: One concrete example, no theory yet

structure.goal: Teach the key idea in plain words
Apply it live on a real case
Repeat the one takeaway and say what to do next

archetypes.name: Myth busting
archetypes.when_to_use: Correcting something most people get wrong.

structure.goal: Name the myth as a bold claim
Explain where the myth comes from
Give the evidence in two beats
Invite a comment with the next myth
Ask the question the viewer already has
Give the two reasons that make it true
Tell them how to use it

hook_styles.example: Why does ice float when almost every solid sinks?
3 steps to read any chart in 10 seconds

hook_styles.pattern: Everything you were taught about [topic] is [wrong or incomplete]
hook_styles.example: Your note-taking method is costing you half of what you read
Most students re-read. Top students do this instead

pacing.notes: Slightly slower than entertainment so terms land; never more than one new term per scene.

shot_conventions.b_roll: the finished result or the surprising object
shot_conventions.note: Look at the lens, no preamble

shot_conventions.b_roll: screen recording or photo of the common mistake
diagram or whiteboard drawing built step by step
shot_conventions.note: Label every element as you draw it

shot_conventions.b_roll: the real example, zoomed on the active area

cta_patterns: Follow for the next lesson in this series
Comment the topic you want explained next
Save this so you can practise later
common_risks: Teaching two ideas in one scene
